corrections: Security review time changed from "up to 4 weeks" to "typically 4–5 weeks", per the live Trailhead security review unit.
The unlisted-package unknown is now a secondary claim: per a search excerpt of Salesforce's packaging guide, unreviewed packages install after an "unauthorized" warning.

name: Salesforce

verdict.headline: You don't need Salesforce review to call the API. To reach customer orgs, build an External Client App, put it in a managed package, and have each customer admin install it.
verdict.nextAction: Enable Dev Hub and register a namespace in a Developer Edition org, then create the External Client App in Setup > External Client App Manager.

appType: Use an External Client App (ECA), not a Connected App. New Connected Apps are disabled by default since Spring '26.

paths.name: Connect customer orgs (managed package, no listing)
paths.whenThisApplies: Your app needs to work in customer orgs other than your own, and you don't need an AppExchange listing.

timeline.note: Hours, by our estimate. No exact range given.

timeline.note: Minutes to weeks, depending on each customer's change control.

beforeApproval.item: In your own org, OAuth (web-server flow + PKCE) works right after you create the ECA. No review is needed.
beforeApproval.detail: A local ECA works only in the org where you create it.

beforeApproval.item: Any customer org can install a managed package containing the ECA from an install link, without AppExchange.
An unreviewed, unlisted package can likely still be installed, but customer admins see an "unauthorized for distribution" warning and must acknowledge it first.
beforeApproval.detail: From a search excerpt of Salesforce's packaging guide. The page itself was blocked, so this is not confirmed.

beforeApproval.item: A legacy Connected App created before Spring '26 still works cross-org and can still be edited.
In customer orgs, a legacy Connected App counts as "uninstalled" until their admin installs it.
beforeApproval.detail: Since Sept 2025, non-admin users can't authorize uninstalled connected apps.

prerequisites.item: Developer Edition org enabled as a Dev Hub, plus a registered namespace (2GP)
prerequisites.detail: The docs say packageable ECAs must be developed in a Dev Hub org.

prerequisites.item: Salesforce CLI and a 2GP managed package
For a listing: a Salesforce partner (ISV) account, Partner Console access, and a listing org
Callback URL(s) over HTTPS and a chosen set of scopes

steps.title: Create the External Client App
steps.detail: In Setup > External Client App Manager, enable OAuth and set the callback URL and scopes. Keep PKCE required (the default), and keep the secret required for refresh. These settings are in the ECA's Policies and Settings.
steps.agentHelp: Draft the scope list with a justification for each scope, plus a settings checklist for the callback URL, PKCE and refresh.

steps.title: Wait about 10 minutes, then test the web-server flow
steps.detail: Test against login.salesforce.com, or test.salesforce.com for sandboxes. The 10-minute figure is from Okta's docs.
steps.agentHelp: Write a step-by-step test script for the web-server flow with PKCE against both login endpoints.

steps.title: Set Distribution State to Packaged and add the ECA to a managed package
steps.detail: Change Distribution State from Local to Packaged. Global OAuth settings, including the consumer secret, are never packaged.

steps.title: Generate the package version, install link and admin install guide
steps.detail: Produce the package version and install link, and write a guide that tells customer admins how to install and assign access.

steps.title: Customer admin installs the app
steps.detail: The customer admin installs the package, or installs the app from Setup > Connected Apps OAuth Usage. If their policy calls for it, they set Permitted Users to admin-approved. They then assign profiles or permission sets.

steps.title: Customer admin allowlists the app (if API Access Control is on)
steps.detail: If the customer has API Access Control on and doesn't allowlist the app, users get blocked.

steps.title: Submit for security review and pay the fee (AppExchange listing only)
steps.detail: Submit the solution for AppExchange (now also called AgentExchange) security review. Trailhead gives the fee for paid solutions as $999 per attempt, including each resubmission. A 2023 blog says free solutions are exempt.
steps.agentHelp: Assemble the submission checklist, and draft the architecture and data-flow docs.

steps.title: Salesforce runs the security review
steps.detail: Trailhead says a solution typically takes 4–5 weeks to get through review. A next-steps email within 2 business days was seen only in a search excerpt.

steps.title: Fix the findings and resubmit
steps.detail: Each resubmission is another attempt and costs another $999.
steps.agentHelp: Draft false-positive documentation for scanner findings and a list of fixes.

submissionChecklist.detail: Keep only the related packages in the review org.
Code Analyzer or Checkmarx, plus a DAST scan for external endpoints.

submissionChecklist.item: False-positive documentation, architecture and data-flow docs

submissionChecklist.detail: $999 per attempt for paid solutions, per Trailhead. A 2023 blog says free solutions are exempt.

gotchas.title: Connected App creation is off by default (Spring '26)
gotchas.detail: Creation is blocked in both the UI and the Metadata API. Support can enable it for now, but Salesforce says that option will be removed. Editing and installing existing Connected Apps still work.

gotchas.title: Users can't authorize uninstalled apps (Sept 2025)
gotchas.detail: Non-admin users can't authorize uninstalled connected apps. Users who already authorized can keep using the app, except with device flow, which is blocked for everyone.

gotchas.title: Bypass permissions are being narrowed
gotchas.detail: The Approve Uninstalled Connected Apps permission is the bypass when API Access Control is off, and Use Any API Client is the bypass when it is on. A later Salesforce article says Use Any API Client will stop allowing self-authorization of uninstalled apps. The rollout was reported to start the week of Dec 8, 2025.

gotchas.title: Local ECAs are not copied to sandboxes on refresh
gotchas.detail: A sandbox refresh does not carry over an ECA whose Distribution State is Local. We found no source for this.

gotchas.title: Professional Edition and some API limits may depend on the partner program
gotchas.detail: Access for Professional Edition orgs and some API limits may depend on the partner program or the security review. Not confirmed.

gotchas.title: Customer admins will see your blocked attempts
gotchas.detail: Spring '26 release notes say blocked attempts to use uninstalled apps are now tracked, so customer admins will see your app in that tracking.

gotchas.title: Each security review attempt costs a fee
gotchas.detail: Trailhead gives the fee for paid solutions as $999 for the first submission and for each later attempt. A 2023 blog says free solutions pay no fee.

blockers.symptom: OAUTH_APPROVAL_ERROR_GENERIC, or the app is blocked
blockers.whatToDo: Have the customer admin install the app or package. Don't ask them to grant broad bypass permissions.

blockers.symptom: You can't create a Connected App
blockers.whatToDo: Use an External Client App. Open a Support case only for a short-term exception.
Fix the findings, pay the retest fee, and resubmit.

How long settings take to propagate, according to help.salesforce.com. The 10-minute figure is from Okta.
Whether the Use Any API Client change is fully enforced.
